subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-user isolation be solved by extending sender-scoped sessions and memory namespaces, by automatic per-user group subagents, or by proving the pattern as an external plugin/SDK experiment first?
rationale: The requested behavior adds durable agent lifecycle, per-user memory and skill boundaries, group message routing policy, and admin/security controls that cannot be chosen safely by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design narrow session and memory isolation first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify sender-scoped session, memory namespace, and skill preference contracts before any automatic group subagent lifecycle is added.

options.title: Sponsor built-in per-user group subagents
options.body: Treat Feishu group subagents as a core bundled Feishu feature and require a broader implementation plan covering lifecycle, quotas, admin commands, and live Feishu security proof.

options.title: Prove as plugin experiment first
options.body: Route the orchestration pattern to an external plugin or ClawHub package and promote only any missing generic SDK seam back to OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Design narrow session and memory isolation first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify sender-scoped session, memory namespace, and skill preference contracts before any automatic group subagent lifecycle is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Feishu dynamic-agent and routing lines blame to this recent area contributor, while the decision spans those exact files and adjacent Feishu subagent hooks.
